rationale: Consolidated the catalog family into one successor crate.
Canonical catalog output is covered as a library contract and fixed-point test rather than a donor dump binary.
Cycle paths and structured diagnostics remain library behavior.
Lock drift is tested through typed findings instead of a dump-only executable.
Iterative deterministic cycle detection and reverse transitive dependents are preserved.
Entries, stable identity metadata, dependencies, material payloads, lookup, and canonical order are preserved under successor naming.
Kind-and-context fallback, fail-closed, and skip decisions are preserved.
The hand parser is replaced by strict serde DTOs with canonical ordering, nested unknown-field rejection, semantic paths, and fixed-point evidence.
The public behavior family is re-exported from a thin successor root.
Canonical lock generation, strict lock codec, and complete drift classification are preserved.
Authority and visual definitions still project into disjoint collision and render types.
Visual, authority-impacting, and structural change impacts and dependent revalidation are preserved.
Duplicate, payload, wrong-kind, missing dependency, cycle, and source-path failures remain typed and gain narrow serializable diagnostics.
Compact voxel material bindings, visual fallback, collision failure, and used-material validation are preserved.
Meaningful codec, cycle, lock, and strict-decoding regressions are consolidated into focused behavior tests; donor text formatting is not an authority.
Material change classification and reload suggestions are asserted structurally rather than through a presentation-only text golden.
Abstract fixture behavior is retained locally without exporting donor test helpers.
The separate protocol crate is consolidated into the behavior owner.
Stored references, catalog/material/lock shapes, stable diagnostic codes, and fallback semantics are exposed narrowly by the owning crate without global vocabulary tables or code generation.

Collision and controller attachment state, activation state, entity lifecycle, effective activity, typed errors, and revisions remain distinct.
Optional transform, bounds, render, collision, containment, controller, asset binding, and kinematic capabilities remain typed data attached through one authoring owner.
Lifecycle and label operations are direct EntityAuthoringService methods with typed receipts and fail-closed optimistic revision checks instead of a universal command enum.
Minimal entity core, terminal tombstones, typed source provenance, ordered labels, scene-node lookup, and durable-save policy are preserved.
Spatial, logical, contained, tooling, lifecycle, attachment, movement, and collision contrasts are covered by focused successor fixtures rather than exported proof data.
Thin roots expose cohesive entity and spatial behavior families without donor runtime topology.
Entity AABB sliding, typed outcomes, first-person pose and collision motion, and centrally scheduled voxel kinematics are conventional spatial services; replay pose hashes are omitted.
Strict full and durable schema-three snapshots preserve all successor state, reject nested unknowns and trailing input, and migrate donor schema two without hand-written proof dumps.
Transform parenting, containment, source ancestry, cycle policy, world transforms, rerooting, and projection-only render grouping remain separate typed relations.

One EntityState owns core and capability tables, direct queries, counts, lifecycle and mutation services, snapshots, and revisions; deterministic replay hash and dump helpers are intentionally excluded.
Full set and translate operations, eligibility, immovable collision policy, validation, projection impact, typed rejection, and one-revision receipts live under TransformService.
Quaternion, translation, scale, transform composition, and AABB-equivalent bounds remain ordinary typed values with full rotation composition.
Presence, activation, lifecycle independence, effective activity, and typed mutation behavior have direct successor regressions.
Pose integration, basis, pitch clamp, collision blocking, look rotation, validation, and one-revision application are retained without replay hash assertions.
State preservation, tombstones, strict codecs, durable filtering, and schema migration are structural assertions; donor byte dumps and replay hashes are proof-only residue.
Logical and spatial capability discipline, lifecycle transitions, retired IDs, labels, tombstones, counts, and durable tooling exclusion remain covered.
Axis-separated collision resolution, sliding, hits, immovable actors, and atomic transform application remain spatial-service behavior.
Distinct relation semantics, cycles, endpoint validation, world propagation, provenance retention, destroy policy, and projection refusal are covered.
Entity AABB obstacle collision remains available alongside the voxel collision projection rather than being mistaken for it.
Transform eligibility, full mutation, static immovability, validation, projection impact, and transform composition remain directly exercised.
The generic service is consolidated with its state owner rather than recreated as a routing crate.
Typed collision and controller activation and projections remain direct authority operations; ECRP rule-owner authorization is obsolete with the removed provider topology.

Generic validation, atomic admission, lifecycle, capability, transform, movement, relationship, and eligibility behavior is retained under named owners; ECRP owner matrices, ProjectBundle bindings, RuntimeSession seams, entity hashes, replay labels, and downstream game-domain adapters are excluded.
Activation acceptance, effective state, missing capability, tombstone, and lifecycle distinctions have successor regressions without owner-routing tests.
Stored entity DTOs and typed operation inputs live with their behavior owner instead of a global protocol crate.

Transform, source, capability, activation, definition, event, rejection, and strict stored shapes are local typed APIs; universal command routing tables, codegen catalogs, ProjectBundle source traces, and health, weapon, policy, spawn, and faction content stay out of generic engine authority.
Distinct stable IDs remain a zero-dependency foundation without a separate border registry crate.
Entity, subject, process, mode, signal, tag, scene, and prefab IDs are distinct u64 newtypes with stable brand output; codecs opt in explicitly and the global BORDER_IDS codegen table is obsolete.
The facade is consolidated with the only authoritative relationship graph.

Typed command constructors, kind and endpoint data, preview, apply, readout, receipts, diagnostics, cycle checks, rerooting, provenance, and projection refusal are retained without a second rule-assignment cell.
The authored scene behavior family is consolidated into one successor crate with direct entity-state admission.
Proof-oriented bootstrap summary formatting is removed; typed plans and receipts expose the useful allocations, instances, lights, and bindings directly.
Canonical scene output remains a strict fixed-point library contract rather than a dump executable.

Deterministic allocation, complete external-reference resolution, marker-relative instances, bootstrap bindings, and atomic admission remain; RuntimeSession, project-bundle routing, content hashes, and replay records do not.
Canonical flat and ergonomic tree forms, hierarchy order, metadata, assets, markers, instances, and generator/catalog bindings are preserved with an ordinary authored revision.
The hand parser is replaced by owner-local strict serde DTOs with nested unknown-field rejection, semantic validation, canonical ordering, trailing-input rejection, and fixed-point tests.
A thin successor root exports the cohesive authored-scene family without runtime topology.
Ambient, directional, point, and spot intent plus range, decay, angles, penumbra, shadow intent, and classified validation remain renderer-neutral authored data.

Object snapshots and typed create, delete, rename, reparent, light, transform, voxel-retarget, and selection operations use explicit revisions instead of document fingerprints and remain clone-validate-swap atomic.
The parallel SpatialSession world, RuntimeSession identity, and state hashes are removed; admitted nodes are ordinary scene-sourced entities in the single EntityState owner.
Scenes reuse the successor full transform and quaternion types, composition, finite/range/unit validation, and parent-derived world transforms rather than defining a competing transform family.
Complete classified validation covers schemas, trees, transforms, asset declarations and kinds, lights, markers, instances, bootstrap bindings, paths, cycles, and supported voxel transforms.
Deterministic allocations, complete reference failures, one-revision admission, and non-mutation on rejection have direct successor regressions without replay evidence.
Typed entity-definition and prefab references, instance identities, markers, resolution context, and marker-relative world placement remain covered.
Canonical round trips, strict nested decoding, semantic rejection, and trailing-input behavior are asserted structurally rather than by proof dumps.
All authored light variants and validation remain available, and admission exposes typed world-space light plans for rendering consumers.
Validated add, reparent, asset, and transform proposals become direct typed scene edits with ordinary optimistic revisions.
Object read models, stale writes, subtree deletion, blank labels, cycles, selection, and atomic failure behavior have successor coverage.
Every admitted scene node still has a transform and hierarchical world pose in EntityState; SpatialSession hashes and replay-only assertions are excluded.
Text summary formatting existed only as proof scaffolding; typed admission receipts are the successor inspection surface.
The separate protocol crate is consolidated with its behavior owner and no code-generation dependency is retained.

Stored scene, transform, light, asset, marker, instance, bootstrap, diagnostic, edit, snapshot, plan, and receipt shapes remain narrow owner APIs; global vocabulary tables, request envelopes, source traces, and replay records are removed.
The persistence and prefab behavior family is consolidated into a successor-owned content crate rather than retaining a generic Asha service lane.
Dump-only proof formatting is removed; deterministic typed load steps are the inspectable API.
A proof executable is unnecessary because canonical manifest bytes and fixed points are directly tested.
Prefab proof dumps are replaced by a strict canonical codec and structural round-trip evidence.
Durable, generated, and cache classes plus cohesive successor roles and exact artifact metadata remain without runtime-role catalogs.
Ordinary SHA-256 content identity replaces the donor proof-oriented short bundle hash.
Handwritten ProjectBundle JSON is replaced by strict owner-local serde with nested unknown and trailing-input rejection.
The thin crate root exposes cohesive content persistence and prefab APIs while omitting ProjectBundle and runtime topology.
Deterministic asset-authority, prefab, scene, entity-state, and resource ordering remains under successor roles.
A generic content manifest retains canonical closure, safe paths, stored identities, cache separation, and validation without becoming an Engine control plane.
Definitions, stable parts and roles, source kinds, one-level variants, typed overrides, full classified validation, and actual resolved composition remain.
The prefab registry now uses strict canonical serde DTOs and validates before construction.
Sorted host-neutral byte and path save plans remain without project compaction policy.

Bounded source admission resolves role, class, length, and hash solely from the manifest and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, cache, oversized, and mismatched bodies; staged runtime handles are obsolete.

Complete prior-to-next write, move, and delete accounting plus exact pre-write authorization and post-publication confirmation remain as host-neutral candidates without ProjectBundle indexes or lock-path special cases.
Meaningful canonical, admission, ordering, transition, stale-write, and failure regressions are asserted structurally instead of by donor text goldens.
Prefab canonical round trips, variant resolution, typed overrides, and unsafe removal diagnostics have focused successor regressions.
Asha-wide ProjectBundle fixture generation is removed; compact owner-level fixtures construct only relevant successor content.
Reusable prefab behavior is retained through small local successor fixtures rather than exported donor test infrastructure.
The offline importer is an ordinary workspace tool consuming only the successor asset and renderer-neutral owners it actually needs.
The supported strict source and offline-only posture are crate-level contracts; Asha naming and runtime assumptions are removed.
Dump-only report proof is removed; the deterministic plan report accompanies typed files and classifications.
Generated native artifacts are directly testable and need no proof dump executable.
Typed diagnostics and stable labels replace a formatting-only executable.
Strict sidecar fixed points, inspection fields, and reconciliation are direct APIs rather than evidence dumps.
Deterministic catalog and static-mesh bytes use the canonical successor codecs and renderer model.
The renamed CLI exposes plan, write, sidecar initialization, and validation without Asha runtime or project commands.
Filesystem-free dry-run planning and verified whole-directory publication replace per-file swaps, preventing partial output on failure.
Stable severity, codes, loci, messages, and remedies remain local to the importer.
SHA-256 source and artifact provenance replaces the donor short FNV fingerprint.
Asha fixture generation is removed; focused inline donor-regression sources cover the supported boundary.
Triangle, stream, index, group, material, texture, collision, scale, and descriptor behavior now produces render-model and asset-catalog values directly.
The custom parser and writer are replaced by strict serde DTOs and canonical owner codecs with trailing-input rejection.
The cohesive offline import family is exposed without any runtime import bridge.
Source, schema, importer, GUID, and artifact provenance plus noop, visual, structural, and lock-drift classifications remain strict and deterministic.
Stable 128-bit GUIDs, four URI kinds, typed settings and project overrides, move/content reconciliation, duplicate detection, and strict canonical codecs remain without project containment.
The strict bounded source-mesh schema retains defaults and classified unsupported-feature rejection while adding unknown-field, non-finite, index, and quota checks.
Source and artifact fingerprints plus reimport/drift classifications integrate with the successor catalog and ordinary lock authority.
Generated catalogs and static meshes pass the actual successor owner validation boundaries.
Deterministic dry-run and whole-directory write behavior is structurally tested without retaining an Asha-branded text golden.
Unsupported features and topology remain classified; focused assertions replace presentation-only diagnostic snapshots.
Artifact and manifest determinism are fixed-point structural contracts rather than copied donor bytes.
Static mesh index width is selected from render-model MeshIndexWidth rather than a duplicated string.
Sidecar canonical round trips, GUID persistence, reconciliation, duplicate detection, and project-override non-mutation have successor regressions.
The stored asset contract and behavior are one independently meaningful successor crate rather than protocol/service halves.

Sparse assets, catalog material bindings, source mappings, provenance, independent voxel/content hashes, bounded palette replacement, and classified validation remain; Asha media types, ProjectBundle paths, runtime-session load/unload receipts, and replay hashes are obsolete.
Annotation data and behavior are consolidated in one host-neutral content owner.

Semantic kinds, sparse regions, parentage, provenance, target identity, query modes, typed edits, export, receipts, and diagnostics remain without runtime-layer IDs, replay evidence, or protocol codegen vocabulary tables.
History is part of the existing voxel authority owner rather than another protocol crate.

Entries, parent chains, cursors, bounded diffs and samples, preview/apply revert, undo/redo, quotas, stale hashes, redo-tail invalidation, and strict durable reconstruction remain; checkpoint references, media types, protocol routing, and replay certification are obsolete.
The thin validation service is consolidated with its data owner.
Strict canonical JSON, sparse overlap and bounds validation, material reference admission, semantic and voxel-data SHA-256 hashes, and fail-atomic palette updates supersede the donor FNV service.
The annotation service is consolidated with the cohesive annotation family.

Target-aware bounded validation, cycle and overlap checks, canonical SHA-256 identities, cell/bounds/region queries, every typed edit family, strict decode, and compare-and-swap export remain without runtime facade state.
Reusable voxel edit behavior extends the existing successor spatial owner and its one collision/navigation/mesh authority.

Bounded cell commands, canonical order, optimistic revisions, atomic multi-edit validation, no-op rejection, off-side projection rebuild, preview/commit, typed facts, and failure non-mutation remain; event replay and donor chunk-residency/generator assumptions are excluded.

Base-state reconstruction, accepted transaction entries, parent chains, cursor and fork behavior, stale-hash rejection, bounded undo/redo/revert, diffs, quotas, and failure non-mutation remain; ProjectBundle compaction and replay proofing are excluded.
Changed counts, inclusive bounds, material transitions, transaction IDs, bounded samples, and truncation remain in direct history receipts.

Strict bounded canonical history snapshots reconstruct base state, cursor, and redo tail with SHA-256 corruption detection; replay logs, generator-version migration, and committed proof goldens are obsolete.

Renderer hints are re-cast through authoritative collision, mismatches fail closed, place/remove anchors are typed, and translated, rotated, non-uniformly scaled instances are transformed and revalidated in Rust.
Conversion data and behavior are consolidated in one offline authoring owner rather than protocol and service halves.

Source identities and metadata, plan/preview/apply requests and receipts, texture sampling, fit/origin/transform settings, and bounded model info/window readouts remain as strict serde models; evidence artifacts, global diagnostic tables, runtime dispatch, session hashes, and replay hashes are obsolete.
Static mesh import is a cohesive part of the offline converter.

Embedded GLB parsing, non-finite/index/topology rejection, source SHA-256, 64 MiB/2M-vertex/6M-index cumulative limits, groups, material slots, bounds, provenance, and strict request decoding remain; conversion continues to reject ambiguous transformed or multiply-instanced scene shapes rather than silently discard them.
Conversion planning and execution extend the existing successor converter without a new runtime service layer.

Real sampled surface and closed-solid conversion, exact resource ceilings, SHA-256 source/settings/plan/output identities, stale guards, bounded preview, fail-atomic apply/install, contain/cover/stretch, source/min/center origins, affine transforms, fallback and texture-sampled materials, and model readouts remain; FNV evidence URIs, runtime authority snapshots, and replay certification are removed.
Deterministic environment generation is a cohesive part of the explicit authoring owner rather than a replay-oriented runtime service.

Bounded tunnel validation, seeded wall/floor/accent cells, marker positions and yaw, centered playable frame, collision-cell bounds, and direct collision/navigation/mesh admission remain; ChunkGenerated replay events, FNV proof records, text goldens, and renderer chunk summaries are obsolete.
Generation and native asset/scene materialization form one independently meaningful offline authoring crate.

Direct typed requests produce bounded canonical voxel assets, revisioned scene candidates, consumed generator bindings, marker mappings, and composed world transforms without ProjectBundle paths, RuntimeSession sources, provider dispatch, replacement proof topology, or artifact-set hashes.
Deterministic kinematic integration extends the existing collision and motion owner rather than adding a service-routing crate.

Tick-derived fixed steps, semi-implicit velocity and position integration, acceleration, gravity scale, zero steps, finite checks, query-required refusal, and sanctioned voxel collision queries remain as direct APIs.
Trigger lifecycle is a cohesive spatial mechanic over object-owned entity capabilities rather than a routed rule crate.

Definition validation, world-space overlap scans, endpoint semantics, enter/continued/exit state, activation and lifecycle cleanup, quotas, and strict snapshot reconstruction remain; RuntimeSession ownership, callback stay events, FNV pair/overlap/snapshot proof hashes, and replay vocabulary are removed.
Generic explicit transition authority remains an independent small crate; animation state remains in the already-complete render-presentation owner.

Deterministic specs, entity-owned instances, allowed transitions, stale-state and revision checks, detached application, ordered iteration, and failure non-mutation remain. Entity eligibility now comes from entity-state; replay strings, DomainEvent bridges, and duplicate animation authority are obsolete.
Detached transition behavior is preserved against the same generic checks and optimistic revision semantics.
